briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 24, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Regression in Global Climate Action and Intensification of the Crisis
sections.content: Recently, Europe has shown a regression in climate change response efforts, a stark contrast to how European nations previously criticized former President Trump [1, 10, 30]. Notably, a survey revealed that a significant number of citizens in six European countries prefer the proliferation of air conditioners over carbon emission reductions, raising concerns that the will to respond might weaken even after severe heatwaves [139]. Amidst this, Colorado is experiencing a surge in heat-related illnesses and the death of centuries-old trees, indicating the intensifying direct impacts of climate change [24, 127]. In the Pacific region, climate change is exacerbating malnutrition and obesity in a complex phenomenon termed a 'global syndemic,' and concerns about the long-term effects of climate change on the Colorado River are also being raised [130, 134]. In Pakistan, the reliance on ice for survival amidst heatwaves reaching up to 50°C due to limited electricity and ventilation facilities starkly illustrates the severity of the climate crisis [140].

sections.title: 🌱 South Korea's Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation Efforts
sections.content: The Republic of Korea is undertaking diverse innovative efforts to address climate change. Notably, the development of an AI-based 'Korean-style Integrated Water Management Platform' is actively underway to proactively respond to droughts and floods, expected to vigorously tackle the climate crisis through water management innovation [2, 14, 18, 21, 31, 33]. In the agricultural sector, researchers from Korea, China, and Japan have gathered in Jeju to study forage crops that thrive despite climate change [6, 12]. Furthermore, Yangpyeong County and the Gyeongbuk region are promoting the on-site dissemination of cultivation techniques for subtropical crops and Korean melons that are resilient to climate change [11, 15, 16]. Additionally, Korea is assisting in the preservation of Ghana's World Heritage castles, which are being damaged by climate change [3], and Kolon FnC is actively contributing to the international community by supporting climate change response education for Mongolian nomads [25, 29, 32].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Expanding Carbon Neutrality Practices
sections.content: Domestic companies are accelerating their transition to renewable energy to achieve carbon neutrality goals. Nexen Tire plans to reduce annual greenhouse gas emissions by 2,700 tons by introducing direct PPAs (Power Purchase Agreements) and expanding solar power facilities at its Yangsan plant, which is also expected to contribute to securing competitiveness in the global finished vehicle supply chain [36, 75, 77, 78, 80, 82, 83, 84, 85, 87, 90, 94, 96, 99, 100, 101, 102, 103, 106, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 114, 116, 117, 118, 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 126]. Investment in renewable energy is also active; Solarbridge is leading renewable energy finance trends by surpassing 200 billion KRW in cumulative P2P loans [74, 86, 107]. Furthermore, Goyang City is actively pursuing eco-friendly energy transition with its citizens through the 'Sunshine Pension' program [89], and the potential for expanding renewable energy is also being confirmed, with the potential for rooftop solar power generation in urban buildings approaching 100 GW [98]. Jeonbuk Technopark is exploring regional energy transition policy directions by hosting a renewable energy policy discussion forum for the 9th popularly elected term [79, 81, 95].

sections.title: 📰 Strategic Realignment and Societal Discussions on Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change has now emerged as a core agenda item for financial sector boards, being recognized not merely as risk management but as a new source of profit generation [7, 17]. Corporations are treating climate change risk types and their countermeasures as key elements of ESG management [13, 63, 66, 72], and changes are being observed in investment strategies, with discussions on prioritizing investments in Canada over Russia due to climate change factors [8]. Domestically, citizen-participatory education and campaigns for practicing carbon neutrality are actively underway; Gwangmyeong City and Gwangju Seogu are conducting carbon neutrality experiential education for children [35, 41, 59, 65], and Daedeok-gu is encouraging daily practices such as eco-friendly gift wrapping using discarded wrapping cloths [38, 47, 52, 57, 58, 62]. Meanwhile, criticisms have been raised that the amendment to the Carbon Neutrality Act is trapped in socioeconomic 'inertia,' alongside calls for carbon neutrality to become industrial competitiveness rather than a burden on the public, suggesting the need for in-depth discussions on policy direction [28, 71]. Internationally, climate change is causing geopolitical shifts, such as providing China with new Arctic shipping routes [132], and new scientific discussions are also emerging, suggesting that 'wind' might be a missing piece in climate change research [135].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the global efforts to address climate change, alongside regressive trends, as well as South Korea's innovative adaptation and mitigation efforts, the acceleration of renewable energy transition, and the importance of strategic realignment across society and citizen participation. This is a time that calls for sustained attention and effort to overcome the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
